supremeCourt.name: Corte Suprema de Justicia — Sala de lo Constitucional
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Magistrates elected by the Legislative Assembly.
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: During the FMLN era (2009–2018) the Constitutional Chamber was notably independent, ruling against both ARENA and FMLN governments. The decisive change came AFTER the FSP era: on 1 May 2021 President Bukele’s Assembly (Nuevas Ideas) removed the 5 Constitutional Chamber magistrates and the Attorney General, replacing them with loyalists; in Sept 2021 the new chamber authorised presidential re-election. This was done by Bukele, not by an FSP president.
supremeCourt.stillServing: The pre-2021 Constitutional Chamber was entirely removed; the Bukele-aligned magistrates installed on 1 May 2021 remain in place.

courtHistory.event: Under the military-authoritarian regimes and the 1979–1992 civil war the court was weak and politically dependent; the 1983 Constitution created the current framework.
The Chapultepec Peace Accords brought judicial reforms; magistrates elected by the Legislative Assembly with opposition input.
The Constitutional Chamber ('Sala 4') was notably independent, issuing landmark rulings against both ARENA and FMLN governments — a high point of judicial autonomy.

On 1 May, President Bukele's new Assembly (Nuevas Ideas) removed the 5 Constitutional Chamber magistrates and the Attorney General, installing loyalists; in Sept 2021 the new chamber authorised presidential re-election. Done by Bukele — NOT an FSP president.

supremeCourt.justicesNote: The 15-magistrate CSJ (incl. the 5-member Constitutional Chamber) was reconstituted in 2021; current members are Bukele-aligned and not itemized here.

current: Frente Farabundo Martí para la Liberación Nacional (FMLN)
fspParties.note: The FMLN is El Salvador's FSP founding member.

legislativeControl.seats: After the 1992 peace accords the FMLN became the main opposition to ARENA — often the largest or second party in the Asamblea, but out of government.
The FMLN held the presidency (Funes, Sánchez Cerén) but never an Assembly majority — it governed as a minority, negotiating with GANA/PCN.
The FMLN collapsed as Nayib Bukele rose; his Nuevas Ideas swept the 2021 Assembly (a supermajority), reducing the FMLN to a handful of seats.

parties.name: Frente Farabundo Martí para la Liberación Nacional

government.note: The FMLN's best-ever result — the largest bloc, but 8 seats short of a majority. The Funes government legislated through shifting deals with the smaller right-of-centre parties (and, from late 2009, the GANA split from ARENA); the FMLN never controlled the Assembly outright in either of its two presidencies (2009–2019).
